title: How GST Taxes Only the Value Added

segments.say: A shirt passes through many hands: farmer, mill, tailor, shop. If each one is taxed on the full price, tax piles on tax.

left.title: Before
items: Tax on the full price at each step

segments.say: That was the old problem, called cascading: tax on tax. GST fixes it by taxing only the value each step adds.

Imagine a ten percent rate. The mill sells cloth for a hundred rupees and pays ten in tax. The tailor sells the shirt for a hundred and fifty: tax fifteen. But the tailor subtracts the ten already paid, and pays just five.

anim.title: Input tax credit
items: Each seller claims the tax already paid
Only the value they added is taxed
The full tax is paid by the final buyer

segments.say: That subtraction is called input tax credit. In the end, the full tax lands on the final buyer, once.
GST came through the hundred-and-first Constitutional Amendment in twenty sixteen, and began on the first of July, twenty seventeen.
Rates are decided by the GST Council, chaired by the Union Finance Minister, with finance ministers of all the states. A rare example of shared decision-making.

For GS Three: GST taxes value added, input tax credit ends tax on tax, and the GST Council under Article two seventy-nine A sets the rates. It is also a good example of cooperative federalism for GS Two.

sources: The Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016: Article 246A, Article 269A and Article 279A (GST Council: Union Finance Minister as chairperson, state finance ministers as members)
CBIC, GST concept and status / FAQs (cbic-gst.gov.in): GST rolled out 1 July 2017; destination-based tax on supply; input tax credit removes the cascading effect
The worked example uses an imaginary 10% rate for arithmetic only

quiz.q: What does input tax credit prevent?
quiz.why: Each seller subtracts tax already paid.

quiz.q: Which Article creates the GST Council?

reviewNote: Facts were read against the 101st Amendment Act and CBIC's GST pages. The 10% example is labelled as imaginary in the narration. Moving facts: GST rate slabs change; none are stated.
